title: Maximum term width bounded iff every term bounded
statement: Let $t_1, \dots, t_k$ be a finite list of terms, each a conjunction of literals, and let $\ell$ be a natural number; write $w(t)$ for the width of a term (its number of literals). Then the maximum width over the list, taken to be $0$ when the list is empty, satisfies $\max_{1 \le i \le k} w(t_i) \le \ell$ if and only if $w(t) \le \ell$ for every term $t$ in the list.
hypotheses_covered: folded maximum of widths (with base value 0)
replaced:
For a list of terms $ts$, the folded maximum of their widths is at most $\ell$ if and
only if every term $t \in ts$ satisfies $t.\mathrm{width} \le \ell$.
